intended_object: The coordinatewise real-part map ℂ³ → ℝ³, a ↦ (Re a₀, Re a₁, Re a₂), as a continuous ℝ-linear map. It is used to take the real part of complex vector-valued sources in the Navier–Stokes construction. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the `realPart_apply` lemma.
explanation:
`ComplexVector` is `Fin 3 → ℂ` and `ProblemStatement.Space` is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`. The body sends `a` to `!₂[(a 0).re, (a 1).re, (a 2).re]`, which is the componentwise real part. The definition proves additivity and ℝ-homogeneity, then turns the linear map into a continuous one with `LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap`, which applies because the domain is finite-dimensional. `realPart_apply` confirms `realPart a i = (a i).re`, and the library uses the map as expected: it decomposes a vector as complexify(re) + i·complexify(im), and it uses the fact that the real part of a conjugate source equals the real part of the source.

Mathlib only has the scalar version, `Complex.reCLM : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ`. It has no named definition of the componentwise real part from ι → ℂ to `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`. In principle the map could be stated for any finite index type. Here, though, it is a concrete bridge between the project's two fixed types: complex 3-vectors and physical space ℝ³. The dimension 3 is part of the Navier–Stokes setting, not an arbitrary restriction of a general Mathlib notion. So the definition is correct and suitably general for what it is meant to do.
